guideline: Visual Turing test: distinguish generated vs ground-truth questions
Object relevance verification with true/adversarial pairs
- Four experiments: visual Turing test, grammatical plausibility, relevance to image, and object relevance judgment.

Humans were asked to (1) choose which of two questions was generated (visual Turing test), (2) judge grammatical naturalness, (3) assess relevance of the generated question to the image, and (4) verify if presented objects were relevant to the question.

Experiment 1 is a visual Turing test: given an image, a model generated question and a ground truth question, we ask a human to determine which question they believe is model generated. Experiment 2 attempts to discern the linguistic and grammatical capabilities of our model by asking a human to make a binary choice about whether the generated question seems natural. Experiment 3 shows a human an image alongside a model generated question (explicit variant). Then, we ask the human to make a choice about whether the generated question is relevant to the image. Finally, experiment 4 judges whether objects are relevant to a generated question.
criteria: ability to distinguish generated vs ground-truth question
